SECTION D: (5 Marks Each)

Q35(A). From the top of a 7 m high building, the angle of elevation of the top of a cable tower is 60° and the angle of depression of its foot is 45°. Determine the height of the tower.
OR
Q35(B). From the top of a 75 m lighthouse, angles of depression of two ships are 30° and 45°. One ship is exactly behind the other on the same side. Find the distance between ships. (Use √3 = 1.732)

Answer / Solution (A):
Let horizontal distance to tower base = d.
From depression 45°: tan45° = 7/d => d = 7 m
From elevation 60°: tan60° = (tower height - 7)/d
=> √3 = (h - 7)/7 => h - 7 = 7√3
So h = 7 + 7√3 = 7(1 + √3)
Using √3 = 1.732: h ≈ 7(2.732) = 19.124 m
Answer: 19.124 m (approx)

Answer / Solution (B):
Let lighthouse height AB = 75 m.
For nearer ship (45°): tan45° = 75/BC => BC = 75 m
For farther ship (30°): tan30° = 75/BD => 1/√3 = 75/BD => BD = 75√3
Distance between ships = BD - BC = 75(√3 - 1)
= 75(1.732 - 1) = 75×0.732 = 54.9 m
Answer: 54.9 m
